compliances.name: Notify a data breach in New Jersey
compliances.head: Data breach notification
compliances.authority: New Jersey Division of State Police
compliances.brief: A business whose computerized records of New Jersey residents' personal information are breached must tell those residents, and must report the breach to the State Police first.
compliances.why: You hold personal information about New Jersey residents.

due.text: In the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay; State Police first

compliances.dueText: Disclosure to a customer in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay. In advance of the disclosure to the customer, report the breach to the Division of State Police. Over 1,000 persons: also notify the consumer reporting agencies without unreasonable delay.
compliances.evidence: The disclosure to a customer shall be made in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay ... shall, in advance of the disclosure to the customer, report the breach of security ... to the Division of State Police
compliances.note: No fixed number of days. Read on the 2019 amending act (official Legislature text), not a consolidated statute.

compliances.name: Notify a data breach in New Mexico
compliances.head: Data breach notification
compliances.authority: New Mexico Attorney General
compliances.brief: A business must notify New Mexico residents whose personal identifying information was breached within 45 days, and tell the Attorney General when more than 1,000 residents are notified.
compliances.why: You hold personal information about New Mexico residents.

due.text: Not later than 45 calendar days after discovery of the breach

compliances.dueText: In the most expedient time possible, but not later than forty-five calendar days following discovery of the security breach. More than 1,000 residents: notify the Attorney General and the major consumer reporting agencies within the same 45 calendar days.
compliances.evidence: be made in the most expedient time possible, but not later than forty-five calendar days following discovery of the security breach
compliances.note: Read on the enacted 2017 bill text on nmlegis.gov; the codified NMSA chapter 57 article 12C on nmonesource.com did not load (script-only page).

compliances.name: Notify a data breach in New York
compliances.head: Data breach notification
compliances.authority: New York Attorney General, Department of State and Division of State Police
compliances.brief: A business whose computerized private information about New York residents is breached must notify them within 30 days, and notify the Attorney General, the Department of State and the State Police (and DFS if it is a covered entity).
compliances.why: You hold personal information about New York residents.

due.text: Within 30 days after the breach has been discovered

compliances.dueText: In the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay, provided that such notification shall be made within thirty days after the breach has been discovered. When any New York residents are notified, also notify the state attorney general, the department of state and the division of state police.
compliances.evidence: The disclosure shall be made in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay, provided that such notification shall be made within thirty days after the breach has been discovered

compliances.name: Notify a data breach in North Carolina
compliances.head: Data breach notification
compliances.authority: North Carolina Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
compliances.brief: A business that owns or licenses personal information of North Carolina residents, in any form, must notify affected people of a breach and also notify the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division.
compliances.why: You hold personal information about North Carolina residents.

due.text: Without unreasonable delay after discovery of the breach

compliances.dueText: The disclosure notification shall be made without unreasonable delay. When notice is given to affected persons, notify the Consumer Protection Division of the Attorney General's Office without unreasonable delay; over 1,000 persons, also the nationwide consumer reporting agencies.
compliances.evidence: The disclosure notification shall be made without unreasonable delay, consistent with the legitimate needs of law enforcement
compliances.note: No fixed number of days.

compliances.name: Notify a data breach in North Dakota
compliances.head: Data breach notification
compliances.authority: North Dakota Attorney General
compliances.brief: A business must tell North Dakota residents whose unencrypted personal information was acquired in a breach, and tell the Attorney General when more than 250 people are affected.
compliances.why: You hold personal information about North Dakota residents.

due.text: In the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay

compliances.dueText: The disclosure must be made in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay. Disclose to the attorney general, by mail or email, any breach exceeding two hundred fifty individuals.
compliances.evidence: shall disclose to the attorney general by mail or electronic mail any breach of the security system which exceeds two hundred fifty individuals. The disclosure must be made in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay
compliances.note: No fixed number of days.

compliances.name: Notify a data breach in Ohio
compliances.head: Data breach notification
compliances.authority: Ohio Attorney General
compliances.brief: A business must notify Ohio residents whose computerized personal information was breached within 45 days. Over 1,000 residents, it also notifies the consumer reporting agencies.
compliances.why: You hold personal information about Ohio residents.

due.text: Not later than 45 days after discovery or notification of the breach

compliances.dueText: In the most expedient time possible but not later than forty-five days following its discovery or notification of the breach. More than 1,000 residents: notify all nationwide consumer reporting agencies without unreasonable delay.
compliances.evidence: The person shall make the disclosure described in division (B)(1) of this section in the most expedient time possible but not later than forty-five days following its discovery or notification of the breach
compliances.note: The statute section read does not require notice to the Attorney General.

compliances.name: Notify a data breach in Oklahoma
compliances.form: Data Security Breach Reporting Form (Attorney General)
compliances.head: Data breach notification
compliances.authority: Oklahoma Attorney General
compliances.brief: A business must notify Oklahoma residents of a breach without unreasonable delay. Since January 1, 2026 it must also tell the Attorney General, within 60 days of notifying residents, when 500 or more residents are affected.
compliances.why: You hold personal information about Oklahoma residents.

due.text: Residents without unreasonable delay; Attorney General no more than 60 days after notifying residents

compliances.dueText: Disclosure shall be made without unreasonable delay. Notice to the Attorney General without unreasonable delay but in no event more than sixty (60) days after providing notice to impacted residents. Breaches affecting fewer than 500 residents (1,000 for a credit bureau) are exempt from the Attorney General notice.
compliances.evidence: shall also provide notice to the Attorney General of such breach without unreasonable delay but in no event more than sixty (60) days after providing notice to impacted residents of this state.

compliances.name: Notify a data breach in Oregon
compliances.head: Data breach notification
compliances.authority: Oregon Department of Justice (Attorney General)
compliances.brief: A business must notify affected consumers within 45 days of discovering a breach, and the Attorney General when more than 250 consumers are notified. A vendor must tell its client within 10 days.
compliances.why: You hold personal information about Oregon residents.

due.text: Not later than 45 days after discovering or being notified of the breach

compliances.dueText: In the most expeditious manner possible, without unreasonable delay, but not later than 45 days after discovering or receiving notification of the breach of security. Notify the Attorney General if more than 250 consumers must be notified.
compliances.evidence: A covered entity shall give notice of a breach of security in the most expeditious manner possible, without unreasonable delay, but not later than 45 days after discovering or receiving notification of the breach of security.

compliances.name: Notify a data breach in Pennsylvania
compliances.head: Data breach notification
compliances.authority: Pennsylvania Office of Attorney General
compliances.brief: A business must notify affected Pennsylvania residents without unreasonable delay, and when more than 500 residents are affected, notify the Attorney General at the same time.
compliances.why: You hold personal information about Pennsylvania residents.

due.text: Without unreasonable delay; Attorney General at the same time when more than 500 residents are affected

compliances.dueText: Notify the affected Pennsylvania resident without unreasonable delay. When more than 500 Pennsylvania residents are affected, notice must be made to the Attorney General at the same time the entity notifies the affected individuals; also notify consumer reporting agencies without unreasonable delay.
compliances.evidence: Entities must notify the Attorney General when more than 500 Pennsylvania residents are affected by a breach. Notice must be made to the Attorney General at the same time the entity notifies the affected individuals.
compliances.note: The 7-business-day deadlines on the same page apply to state agencies and state contractors, not to ordinary businesses.

compliances.name: Notify a data breach in Rhode Island
compliances.head: Data breach notification
compliances.authority: Rhode Island Attorney General
compliances.brief: A business must notify affected Rhode Island residents within 45 calendar days of confirming a breach, and the Attorney General and credit reporting agencies when more than 500 residents are notified.
compliances.why: You hold personal information about Rhode Island residents.

due.text: No later than 45 calendar days after confirmation of the breach

compliances.dueText: In the most expedient time possible, no later than forty-five (45) calendar days after confirmation of the breach and the ability to ascertain the information required for the notice. More than 500 residents: also notify the attorney general and the major credit reporting agencies.
compliances.evidence: no later than forty-five (45) calendar days after confirmation of the breach and the ability to ascertain the information required to fulfill the notice requirements

compliances.name: Report new hires to New Jersey
compliances.form: New hire report (W-4 or state form)
compliances.head: New-hire reporting
compliances.authority: New Jersey Child Support Employer Services Portal (NJ Division of Family Development)
compliances.brief: Every employer reports each new, re-hired or returning employee to New Jersey's new-hire directory, which uses it to collect child support.
compliances.why: You hire employees in New Jersey.

due.text: Within 20 days after the employee is hired, re-hired or returns to work

compliances.dueText: Within 20 days of the hiring, re-hiring or return to work of the employee. An employer that sends its reports magnetically or electronically reports every 15 days.
compliances.penalty: A written warning for the first violation; after that a civil penalty of not more than $25 per violation, or $500 where the employer and the employee conspire not to report or to give a false or incomplete report.
compliances.evidence: shall submit the information required in this subsection within 20 days of the hiring, re-hiring, return to work, or contracting of the employee or person ... except that an employer or other entity who transmits reports magnetically or electronically shall report every 15 days
compliances.note: Read in the statute on 2026-11-12. The state's child support page (njchildsupport.gov) gives the same 20 days.

compliances.name: Report new hires to New Mexico
compliances.head: New-hire reporting
compliances.authority: New Mexico Health Care Authority
compliances.brief: Employers report every newly hired or re-hired employee, full-time, part-time or temporary, to the New Mexico New Hire Directory.
compliances.why: You hire employees in New Mexico.

due.text: Within 20 days of the hire date

compliances.dueText: Newly hired and/or rehired employees must be reported within 20 days of their hire date, whether full-time, part-time or temporary.
compliances.evidence: Newly hired and/or rehired employees must be reported within 20 days of their hire date, whether they are considered full-time, part-time, or temporary employees.
compliances.note: Neither page read states a penalty amount.

compliances.name: Report new hires to New York
compliances.head: New-hire reporting
compliances.authority: New York State Department of Taxation and Finance
compliances.brief: Employers report newly hired or rehired employees who will work in New York, and independent contractors with contracts over $2,500, to the Department of Taxation and Finance.
compliances.why: You hire employees in New York.

due.text: Within 20 calendar days of the hiring date

compliances.dueText: Within 20 calendar days from the hiring date. For a nonresident visa employee, 20 calendar days from the date the employee receives a Social Security number.
compliances.penalty: $20 for each employee not reported on time, and $20 for each false or incomplete report.
compliances.evidence: You must report newly hired or rehired employees who will be employed in New York State within 20 calendar days from the hiring date.

compliances.name: Report new hires to North Carolina
compliances.head: New-hire reporting
compliances.authority: North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services (State Directory of New Hires)
compliances.brief: Every employer reports the hiring of each employee who fills in a federal W-4 to the North Carolina State Directory of New Hires.
compliances.why: You hire employees in North Carolina.

due.text: Not later than 20 days from the date of hire

compliances.dueText: Not later than 20 days from the date of hire, or, for electronic filers, by two monthly transmissions not less than 12 nor more than 16 days apart.
compliances.penalty: A civil penalty of up to $25; up to $500 if the failure results from a conspiracy between employer and employee.
compliances.evidence: The employer shall report the information required under this section not later than 20 days from the date of hire

compliances.name: Report new hires to North Dakota
compliances.head: New-hire reporting
compliances.authority: North Dakota Health and Human Services, Child Support
compliances.brief: Employers report all newly hired employees, full-time, part-time and temporary, adult and minor, to the North Dakota State Directory of New Hires.
compliances.why: You hire employees in North Dakota.

due.text: Within 20 days of the employee's first day of work

compliances.dueText: Within 20 days of the employee's first day of work.
compliances.penalty: Civil money penalties set by NDCC § 34-15-05 and § 34-15-06 (amount not stated on the page).
compliances.evidence: Federal and state laws require all employers to report all newly hired employees to the State Directory of New Hires within 20 days of the employee's first day of work.

compliances.name: Report new hires to Ohio
compliances.head: New-hire reporting
compliances.authority: Ohio Department of Job and Family Services
compliances.brief: Every employer reports each newly hired employee, and each contractor it engages, who lives or works in Ohio to the Department of Job and Family Services.
compliances.why: You hire employees in Ohio.

due.text: Not later than 20 days after the date of hire

compliances.dueText: Not later than twenty days after the date on which the employer hires an employee or engages or re-engages a contractor.
compliances.penalty: $25 for each failure to make a report; $500 for each failure that results from a conspiracy between employer and employee.
compliances.evidence: An employer shall make the new hire report not later than twenty days after the date on which the employer hires an employee or the date on which the employer engages or re-engages the contractor
compliances.note: Read on the Ohio Revised Code; the state reporting site oh-newhire.com refused automated access (403).

compliances.name: Report new hires to Oklahoma
compliances.head: New-hire reporting
compliances.authority: Oklahoma Employment Security Commission
compliances.brief: All newly hired employees are reported to the Oklahoma Employment Security Commission.
compliances.why: You hire employees in Oklahoma.

due.text: Within 20 days of the employee's start date

compliances.dueText: All newly hired employees must be reported to OESC within 20 days of a new employee's start date.
compliances.evidence: All newly hired employees must be reported to OESC within 20 days of a new employee's start date.
compliances.note: The page does not state a penalty.

compliances.name: Report new hires to Oregon
compliances.head: New-hire reporting
compliances.authority: Oregon Department of Justice, Child Support Program
compliances.brief: Employers report all new hires and rehires, and newly engaged or re-engaged independent contractors, to the Oregon Child Support Program.
compliances.why: You hire employees in Oregon.

due.text: Within 20 days of the hire date

compliances.dueText: Report all new hires and rehires within 20 days of the hire date; newly engaged and reengaged independent contractors within the same timeframe.
compliances.evidence: Oregon law requires employers to report all new hires and rehires of employees to the Oregon Child Support Program within 20 days of the hire date.
compliances.note: The page does not state a penalty.

compliances.name: Report new hires to Pennsylvania
compliances.head: New-hire reporting
compliances.authority: Pennsylvania Department of Labor & Industry (PA CareerLink)
compliances.brief: All employers with employees in Pennsylvania report each new hire, and rehires after more than 30 days without pay, to the Pennsylvania New Hire Reporting Program.
compliances.why: You hire employees in Pennsylvania.

due.text: Within 20 days of the date of hire (the first day services are performed for wages)

compliances.dueText: Employers must report their new hires to the Program within twenty (20) days of the Date of Hire, the first day services are performed for wages.
compliances.evidence: The Date Of hire is the first day services are performed for wages by the individual. Employers must report their new hires to the Program within twenty (20) days of the Date of Hire.
compliances.note: The page does not state a penalty.

compliances.name: Report new hires to Rhode Island
compliances.head: New-hire reporting
compliances.authority: Rhode Island New Hire Reporting Directory (Office of Child Support Services)
compliances.brief: Employers report all new hires and rehires to the Rhode Island New Hire Registry. Rhode Island's deadline is shorter than most states'.
compliances.why: You hire employees in Rhode Island.

due.text: Within 14 days after hire or rehire

compliances.dueText: Not later than 14 days after hire or rehire. Employers that report electronically or magnetically send two monthly transmissions not less than 12 days nor more than 15 days apart.
compliances.evidence: must report the hiring or rehiring of the employee to the department or its designee not later than fourteen (14) days after hire or rehire if reporting on a W-4 or its equivalent ... by two (2) monthly transmissions not less than twelve (12) days, nor more than fifteen (15) days apart
compliances.note: Read in the statute on 2026-11-12. The section states no penalty.

compliances.name: Register for RetireReady NJ (or certify an exemption): 10 to 19 employees
compliances.head: State retirement programme
compliances.authority: New Jersey Department of the Treasury, RetireReady NJ
compliances.brief: New Jersey employers with ten or more employees that do not offer a qualified retirement plan must facilitate the state's RetireReady NJ savings programme: register, add employees and send payroll deductions. Employers with their own plan certify an exemption.
compliances.why: You employ 10 to 19 people in New Jersey and offer no qualified retirement plan.
compliances.dueText: February 17, 2027: the registration deadline for employers with 10 to 19 employees.
compliances.evidence: "Every New Jersey employer with ten or more employees must facilitate the program" "February 17, 2027" "Employers with 10 to 19 employees"
compliances.note: Employers that provide their own qualified retirement plan are asked to certify their exemption with the access code they were sent; that is not modelled here. The page read does not state a penalty.

compliances.name: Register for RetireReady NJ (or certify an exemption): 20 to 24 employees
compliances.head: State retirement programme
compliances.authority: New Jersey Department of the Treasury, RetireReady NJ
compliances.brief: New Jersey employers with ten or more employees that do not offer a qualified retirement plan must facilitate the state's RetireReady NJ savings programme: register, add employees and send payroll deductions. Employers with their own plan certify an exemption.
compliances.why: You employ 20 to 24 people in New Jersey and offer no qualified retirement plan.
compliances.dueText: December 1, 2026: the registration deadline for employers with 20 to 24 employees.
compliances.evidence: "Every New Jersey employer with ten or more employees must facilitate the program" "December 1, 2026" "Employers with 20 to 24 employees"
compliances.note: Employers that provide their own qualified retirement plan are asked to certify their exemption with the access code they were sent; that is not modelled here. The page read does not state a penalty.

compliances.name: Register for RetireReady NJ (or certify an exemption): 25 to 39 employees
compliances.head: State retirement programme
compliances.authority: New Jersey Department of the Treasury, RetireReady NJ
compliances.brief: New Jersey employers with ten or more employees that do not offer a qualified retirement plan must facilitate the state's RetireReady NJ savings programme: register, add employees and send payroll deductions. Employers with their own plan certify an exemption.
compliances.why: You employ 25 to 39 people in New Jersey and offer no qualified retirement plan.
compliances.dueText: November 15, 2024: the registration deadline for employers with 25 to 39 employees. This deadline has passed: register now.
compliances.evidence: "Every New Jersey employer with ten or more employees must facilitate the program" "November 15, 2024" "Employers with 25 to 39 employees" "Larger employers, your deadlines have passed. Take action today!"
compliances.note: Employers that provide their own qualified retirement plan are asked to certify their exemption with the access code they were sent; that is not modelled here. The page read does not state a penalty.

compliances.name: Register for RetireReady NJ (or certify an exemption): 40 or more employees
compliances.head: State retirement programme
compliances.authority: New Jersey Department of the Treasury, RetireReady NJ
compliances.brief: New Jersey employers with ten or more employees that do not offer a qualified retirement plan must facilitate the state's RetireReady NJ savings programme: register, add employees and send payroll deductions. Employers with their own plan certify an exemption.
compliances.why: You employ 40 or more people in New Jersey and offer no qualified retirement plan.
compliances.dueText: September 15, 2024: the registration deadline for employers with 40 or more employees. This deadline has passed: register now.
compliances.evidence: "Every New Jersey employer with ten or more employees must facilitate the program" "September 15, 2024" "Employers with 40 or more employees" "Larger employers, your deadlines have passed. Take action today!"
compliances.note: Employers that provide their own qualified retirement plan are asked to certify their exemption with the access code they were sent; that is not modelled here. The page read does not state a penalty.

compliances.name: New Jersey quarterly wage report (WR-30) and contribution report (NJ-927)
compliances.head: Unemployment insurance
compliances.authority: New Jersey Department of Labor and Workforce Development, Division of Employer Accounts
compliances.brief: Every quarter, employers file Form WR-30 listing each employee's wages and base weeks, and Form NJ-927 with the contributions due, both electronically.
compliances.why: You pay employees in New Jersey.
compliances.dueText: File the Employer Report of Wages Paid (WR-30) within 30 days of the end of each calendar quarter. Employers with only household workers file once a year, by January 30.
compliances.penalty: For each employee not reported, reported late or incompletely: $5 for the first failure in eight consecutive quarters, $10 for the second, $25 for the third or later.
compliances.evidence: If you are an employer subject to the law, you must file an "Employer Report of Wages Paid" (WR-30) form within 30 days of the end of each calendar quarter.
compliances.note: The NJ-927 also carries the employer and worker contributions for New Jersey temporary disability and family leave insurance. The handbook page read states the WR-30 deadline; the NJ-927 date was not separately stated on it.

compliances.name: New Mexico quarterly wage and contribution report
compliances.form: Employer's Quarterly Wage and Contribution Report
compliances.head: Unemployment insurance
compliances.authority: New Mexico Department of Workforce Solutions
compliances.brief: Employers file a wage and contribution report online every quarter, even when no wages were paid, and pay the unemployment contributions due.
compliances.why: You pay employees in New Mexico.
compliances.dueText: On or before the last day of the month immediately following the end of the calendar quarter; if that is a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday, the next department business day.
compliances.penalty: $50 if the report is not filed within 10 days after the due date; an additional 5% (at least $25) on contributions not paid in full within 10 days after the due date.
compliances.evidence: An employer's wage and contribution report must be filed electronically on the department's web page on or before the last day of the month immediately following the end of the calendar quarter.

compliances.name: New York quarterly combined withholding, wage reporting and unemployment insurance return
compliances.head: Unemployment insurance
compliances.authority: New York State Department of Labor
compliances.brief: Every covered employer files Form NYS-45 each quarter, even with no payroll, reporting wages, unemployment insurance contributions and New York income tax withheld.
compliances.why: You pay employees in New York.
compliances.dueText: April 30, July 31, October 31 and January 31 for the quarters ending March 31, June 30, September 30 and December 31. You may file on the next business day when the due date falls on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday.
compliances.penalty: Penalties and interest apply; interest on overdue unemployment insurance contributions is 12% a year, and contributions paid more than 60 days late are not credited for rate purposes.
compliances.evidence: Every covered employer must file NYS-45 Quarterly Return, even if the employer had no payroll in the quarter. ... January 1 through March 31 April 30
compliances.note: The NYS-45 also carries New York withholding tax, which us-states.ts may already cover under withholding; this item is the unemployment-insurance wage report side.

compliances.name: North Carolina quarterly tax and wage report
compliances.form: NCUI 101 (Employer's Quarterly Tax and Wage Report)
compliances.head: Unemployment insurance
compliances.authority: North Carolina Division of Employment Security
compliances.brief: Employers file a quarterly unemployment tax and wage report with the Division of Employment Security and pay the tax due.
compliances.why: You pay employees in North Carolina.
compliances.dueText: Quarterly Tax and Wage Reports are due by the last day of the month following the end of each quarter. If the due date falls on a weekend or a holiday, the due date will be the first working day after.
compliances.penalty: Late filing: 5% of the tax due per month, up to 25%. Late payment: 10% of the tax due. Interest also applies.
compliances.evidence: Quarterly Tax and Wage Reports are due by the last day of the month following the end of each quarter.

compliances.name: North Dakota quarterly contribution and wage report
compliances.head: Unemployment insurance
compliances.authority: Job Service North Dakota
compliances.brief: Employers file a contribution and wage report every quarter and pay the unemployment tax due. Employers reporting more than 24 employees must file electronically.
compliances.why: You pay employees in North Dakota.
compliances.dueText: By the end of the month following the quarter: April 30, July 31, October 31 and January 31. If the due date falls on a weekend or a holiday, it moves to the next business day.
compliances.penalty: 5% of contributions due for each month or part of a month until filed; at least $25 for the first late report in a calendar year and $100 for later ones; at most $500 per report.
compliances.evidence: Quarterly reports must be completed and returned with the taxes due by the end of the month following the quarter as indicated below: January 1 - March 31 April 30

compliances.name: Ohio quarterly contribution and wage report
compliances.head: Unemployment insurance
compliances.authority: Ohio Department of Job and Family Services
compliances.brief: Every contributory employer files a quarterly unemployment contribution and wage report electronically, listing each employee's pay.
compliances.why: You pay employees in Ohio.
compliances.dueText: Not later than the last day of the first month following the close of the calendar quarter.
compliances.penalty: A forfeiture of 0.25% of total remuneration reported, at least $50 and at most $1,000.
compliances.evidence: The quarterly report shall be filed not later than the last day of the first month following the close of the calendar quarter for which the quarterly report is being filed.
compliances.note: Read on the Ohio Revised Code and Administrative Code; jfs.ohio.gov pages returned 404.

compliances.name: Oklahoma quarterly contribution and wage report
compliances.head: Unemployment insurance
compliances.authority: Oklahoma Employment Security Commission
compliances.brief: Employers report contributions and wages paid through the OESC Employer Portal every quarter, even when no wages were paid.
compliances.why: You pay employees in Oklahoma.
compliances.dueText: On or before the last day of the month following the calendar quarter to be reported.
compliances.penalty: If not filed within 15 days of the Notice of Non-Receipt (OES-054): $200 plus 10% of total contributions due for experience-rated employers; interest 1% a month.
compliances.evidence: Each employer shall report both contributions and "wages paid" ... through the Employer Portal ... on or before the last day of the month following the calendar quarter to be reported.

compliances.name: Oregon quarterly combined payroll tax report
compliances.head: Unemployment insurance
compliances.authority: Oregon Employment Department and Department of Revenue
compliances.brief: Form OQ reports, each quarter, wages for unemployment insurance, Paid Leave Oregon contributions, and state withholding and transit taxes.
compliances.why: You pay employees in Oregon.
compliances.dueText: 2026: April 30, July 31, November 2, 2026 and February 1, 2027. If the due date is on a weekend or holiday, the report is due the next business day.
compliances.penalty: UI late filing (more than 10 days late after a warning or penalty in the past 3 years): $11 per employee reported, minimum $100, maximum $2,800. Paid Leave late filing: 2% of employee wages. DOR: 5% late payment, plus 20% if more than a month late.
compliances.evidence: 1st — Jan–Feb–Mar March 31, 2026 April 30, 2026 ... 3rd — Jul–Aug–Sep September 30, 2026 November 2, 2026 ... If the due date is on a weekend or holiday, the report is due the next business day.
compliances.note: The same Form OQ is the Paid Leave Oregon quarterly report, so no separate pfml item is listed for Oregon.

compliances.name: Pennsylvania quarterly unemployment compensation wage and tax report
compliances.head: Unemployment insurance
compliances.authority: Pennsylvania Department of Labor & Industry
compliances.brief: Employers file quarterly wage and tax reports electronically in the Unemployment Compensation Management System and pay employer and employee contributions.
compliances.why: You pay employees in Pennsylvania.
compliances.dueText: Reports and contributions are due at the end of the month following the calendar quarter (April 30, July 31, October 31 and January 31). If a due date falls on a weekend or legal holiday, the report is due the next business day.
compliances.penalty: 15% of the total contributions payable for the quarter, minimum $125, maximum $450. Interest accrues on unpaid contributions.
compliances.evidence: Reports and contributions are due at the end of the month following the calendar quarter (April 30, July 31, October 31, and January 31).

compliances.name: Rhode Island quarterly tax and wage report
compliances.head: Unemployment insurance
compliances.authority: Rhode Island Department of Labor and Training
compliances.brief: Employers file the TX-17 each quarter for employment security, job development fund and temporary disability insurance taxes, with each employee's wages.
compliances.why: You pay employees in Rhode Island.
compliances.dueText: Last business day of April, July, October and January.
compliances.penalty: $25 for failure to file the quarterly tax report and 10% for failure to pay contributions to each fund, with interest at 1.5% a month; $25 for late wage information plus $25 a month, up to $200 per report.
compliances.evidence: Employment Security Income Tax Job Development Fund Tax Temporary Disability Insurance Tax TX-17 Last business day of April, July, October, and January. RI Department of Labor and Training
compliances.note: Due date read on the Department of State's business-tax page (revised 03/2026); the DLT Employer Tax Unit pages refused automated access (403). The dates shown are the last weekday of April, July, October and January; a public holiday on that day would make the last business day earlier still. The TX-17 also carries Rhode Island TDI contributions.

compliances.name: New Jersey unclaimed property report
compliances.head: Unclaimed property
compliances.authority: New Jersey Department of the Treasury, Unclaimed Property Administration
compliances.brief: A business holding money or property owed to someone it cannot reach after the dormancy period reports it and pays it over to the State Treasurer each year. Before filing, it must write to owners of items of $50 or more.
compliances.why: You hold unclaimed money or property belonging to others.
compliances.dueText: Reports of personal property must be postmarked before November 1, covering July 1 to June 30. Life insurance property: before May 1, covering the calendar year. Due-diligence letter (certified mail, items of $50 or more): not more than 120 and not less than 60 days before the report.
compliances.penalty: Interest plus a civil penalty of $200 for each day the report, payment or delivery is withheld, up to $100,000.
compliances.evidence: Reports containing personal property must be postmarked before November 1st covering the previous reporting cycle (July 1st through June 30th).
compliances.note: Due set to October 31 because the report must be postmarked BEFORE November 1. Life insurers: before May 1.

compliances.name: New Mexico unclaimed property report
compliances.form: Holder report (negative report RPD-41205 if nothing to report)
compliances.head: Unclaimed property
compliances.authority: New Mexico Taxation and Revenue Department
compliances.brief: Businesses holding unclaimed money or property report and remit it to the Unclaimed Property Office each year, after sending written notice to the owner.
compliances.why: You hold unclaimed money or property belonging to others.
compliances.dueText: On or before November 1 of each year for the twelve months next preceding July 1; life insurance companies on or before May 1 for the preceding calendar year. Written notice to the owner not more than 120 days before filing.
compliances.penalty: Interest, plus a civil penalty of $100 a day, up to $5,000; higher penalties for wilful failure or fraud.
compliances.evidence: Reports must be filed on or before November 1 of each year for the twelve months next preceding July 1 of that year, but a report with respect to a life insurance company must be filed on or before May 1

compliances.name: New York unclaimed funds report
compliances.form: Final report with Verification and Checklist (AC2709)
compliances.head: Unclaimed property
compliances.authority: Office of the New York State Comptroller, Office of Unclaimed Funds
compliances.brief: Businesses report and remit funds that became dormant by December 31 to the State Comptroller, after mailing owners first-class and, for larger amounts, by certified mail.
compliances.why: You hold unclaimed money or property belonging to others.
compliances.dueText: Final report, Verification and Checklist and remittance received by close of business March 10. First-class mailing completed by December 10; certified mailing completed by January 10; dormancy cut-off December 31.
compliances.penalty: $100 for each day a report or affidavit is wilfully delayed or withheld (APL section 1412).
compliances.evidence: December 10 First-class mailing completed ... January 10 Certified mailing completed ... March 10 Final report, Verification and Checklist and remittance received in our office by the close of business
compliances.note: Dates are for general business entities; banks, insurers, brokers and other industries have their own reference sheets.

compliances.name: North Carolina unclaimed property report
compliances.head: Unclaimed property
compliances.authority: North Carolina Department of State Treasurer (NCCash)
compliances.brief: Businesses report and remit unclaimed property to the State Treasurer each year, after mailing owners a notice within a set window before the due date.
compliances.why: You hold unclaimed money or property belonging to others.
compliances.dueText: By November 1 each year for the prior fiscal year (July 1 to June 30); life insurance companies by May 1 for the prior calendar year. Notices mailed not more than 120 or less than 60 days from the reporting due date.
compliances.penalty: Daily interest, a $1,000 civil penalty for each day the report is held, plus 25% of the value of property that should be reported (G.S. 116B-77).
compliances.evidence: All holders, except life insurance companies, must file their unclaimed property reports by November 1 of each year for the prior fiscal year (July 1 – June 30).
compliances.note: G.S. 116B-60(d) says 'before November 1'. The notice threshold is $50 ($25 for securities) until December 1, 2026, then $25 for all property. The Department's page says "by November 1"; the date shown is October 31, the last day that is "before November 1".

compliances.name: North Dakota unclaimed property report
compliances.head: Unclaimed property
compliances.authority: North Dakota Department of Trust Lands, Unclaimed Property Division
compliances.brief: Businesses holding property presumed abandoned report it to the state each year, after sending the owner a first-class notice for items of $25 or more.
compliances.why: You hold unclaimed money or property belonging to others.
compliances.dueText: Before November first of each year, covering the twelve months preceding July first; life insurance companies before May first for the preceding calendar year. Owner notice not more than 120 days before filing.
compliances.penalty: Interest at 1% per 30 days, and a civil penalty of $200 a day, up to $5,000; up to $1,000 a day (max $25,000) plus 25% of the value for evasion.
compliances.evidence: the report under section 47-30.2-21 must be filed before November first of each year and cover the twelve months preceding July first of that year.
compliances.note: Read on the statute; the Unclaimed Property Division site is a script-only app that returned no readable text. Due set to October 31 because the law says 'before November first'.

compliances.name: Ohio unclaimed funds report
compliances.head: Unclaimed property
compliances.authority: Ohio Department of Commerce, Division of Unclaimed Funds
compliances.brief: Holders of unclaimed funds report them to the Division of Unclaimed Funds each year. Before filing, they mail each owner of an item of $50 or more (certified mail for $1,000 or more).
compliances.why: You hold unclaimed money or property belonging to others.
compliances.dueText: Before the first day of November of each year as of the preceding June 30; holders providing life insurance coverage before the first day of May as of the preceding December 31. The owner notice states the funds will be reported thirty days after mailing.
compliances.evidence: The report shall be filed before the first day of November of each year as of the preceding thirtieth day of June
compliances.note: The penalty section was not read. The Department of Commerce news page returned 404.

compliances.name: Oklahoma unclaimed property report
compliances.form: Report of Unclaimed Property (497-UP-2) with notarized Verification of Report
compliances.head: Unclaimed property
compliances.authority: Oklahoma State Treasurer
compliances.brief: Every business entity reports unclaimed property to the State Treasurer each year, after sending owners of items of $50 or more a written notice.
compliances.why: You hold unclaimed money or property belonging to others.
compliances.dueText: All business entities, except life insurance companies, must report annually prior to November 1; life insurance companies prior to May 1. Due diligence notice not more than 120 days before filing, for each property of $50 or more.
compliances.evidence: All business entities, except for life insurance companies, must report unclaimed property annually prior to November 1.
compliances.note: The page read does not state a penalty.

compliances.name: Oregon unclaimed property report
compliances.head: Unclaimed property
compliances.authority: Oregon State Treasury, Unclaimed Property Program
compliances.brief: Holders report property presumed abandoned to the State Treasurer each year, after trying to reach the owner at least 60 days before filing.
compliances.why: You hold unclaimed money or property belonging to others.
compliances.dueText: After October 1, but no later than November 1, of each year for accounts dormant as of June 30. Due diligence to find the owner at least 60 days before filing.
compliances.penalty: For wilful failure, up to $1,000 for individuals and $50,000 for corporations (ORS 98.992), after at least one reporting cycle and written instructions.
compliances.evidence: the holder shall file the report after October 1, but no later than November 1, of each year for accounts dormant as of June 30.
compliances.note: Read on the statute; unclaimed.oregon.gov is a script-only app that returned no readable text.

compliances.name: Pennsylvania unclaimed property report
compliances.head: Unclaimed property
compliances.authority: Pennsylvania Treasury
compliances.brief: Holders report and remit unclaimed property to the Pennsylvania Treasury every spring, after sending owners of property of $50 or more a notice.
compliances.why: You hold unclaimed money or property belonging to others.
compliances.dueText: Reports, property and remittance are due by April 15; Treasury accepts reports from January 1. Owner notice not more than 120 days nor less than 60 days before the due date.
compliances.penalty: Interest at 12% a year, and penalties if warranted under Section 1301.24.
compliances.evidence: Reports, property, and/or remittance are due by April 15, 2026. Treasury will accept reports beginning January 1 through April 15.

compliances.name: Rhode Island unclaimed property report
compliances.head: Unclaimed property
compliances.authority: Rhode Island Office of the General Treasurer
compliances.brief: Holders of property presumed abandoned report it to the General Treasurer each year, after writing to owners of property of $50 or more.
compliances.why: You hold unclaimed money or property belonging to others.
compliances.dueText: Before November 1 of each year as of June 30 next preceding (life insurance companies on the same date). Owner notice not more than 120 days before filing.
compliances.evidence: The report must be filed before November 1 of each year as of June 30, next preceding
compliances.note: The Treasury's own pages refused automated access (403). Penalty section not read.
